item: Federal tax character of Kalshi event contracts
detail: No IRS ruling, revenue procedure, or notice classifies Kalshi event contracts as section 1256 contracts. Practitioners disagree: some take 60/40 treatment on Form 6781, others report capital-asset or ordinary treatment; Kalshi's own tax documentation is limited to 1099-INT, 1099-MISC, 1099-B (crypto transfers), 1099-DA, and a P&L statement, and Kalshi states its information is not tax advice. The Bipartisan Policy Center (Aug 2026) documents the unresolved uncertainty. Impact on healthcare eligibility: none - under any characterization the gains are unearned investment income included in MAGI. Consult a tax professional.
notes: Value intentionally left blank: no official source confirms a single tax character. If section 1256 applies, see IRS Form 6781 (60/40, mark-to-market).

item: Do hours spent trading on Kalshi count as qualifying work?
detail: The CMS rule's work activity includes self-employment per official state Medicaid implementation materials (e.g., Louisiana LDH lists self-employment, unpaid work, internships), and DHCS's letter says work at any kind of job. No official source addresses whether hours spent personally trading event contracts or futures on one's own account qualify as self-employment work. Confirm with the county Medi-Cal office before relying on trading hours.
source_name: Louisiana Dept. of Health - Medicaid work requirements
notes: Verified alternatives that need no earned income: the $580/month any-source income standard, 80 hours/month of community service, or at least half-time school enrollment.

item: Effective-date framing differs across official sources
detail: CMS: states must implement no later than January 1, 2027 (or earlier at state option). CRS Report R48755: effective beginning December 31, 2026, or sooner at state option. DHCS member outreach letter (Aug 2026): the rules will not go into effect until March 2027 (existing members are assessed at six-month renewals, which begin March 1, 2027 in California). These are consistent in practice - coverage months governed by the requirement begin with January 2027, and existing members are first assessed at renewal - but the differing phrasing is flagged for review.
notes: Compare CRS R48755 (congress.gov) and DHCS MEDIL I26-25 (dhcs.ca.gov).

value: Exemption is for caregivers of a child 13 or younger
detail: CMS fact sheet: parents, guardians, caretaker relatives, or family caregivers of a dependent child 13 years of age and under. DHCS member page: parents and caregivers of children ages 0-13. DHCS MEDIL I25-18: parents or caregivers of dependent children aged 14 and above must engage (i.e., 13 and under exempt). However, the DHCS Tracking page phrases it as adults without children under 13 - which read literally would wrongly exclude parents of 13-year-olds. Flagged as a wording inconsistency in one DHCS page.
notes: See also DHCS Tracking Federal Impact page (dhcs.ca.gov/tracking-federal-impact-medi-cal-eligibility/).

item: $580 income-standard wording differs across DHCS materials
value: Income from any source vs. work at a job and earn
detail: DHCS MEDIL outreach letter (operative county instruction): have an income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes). DHCS member-facing Medi-Cal Changes page: work at a job and earn at least $580 a month. CMS fact sheet: have monthly income that is not less than the federal minimum wage multiplied by 80 hours. The narrower member-page phrasing conflicts with the MEDIL; the MEDIL county instruction is the operative guidance. Flagged for review.
notes: Compare the DHCS Medi-Cal Changes page (dhcs.ca.gov/medi-cal/updates/medi-cal-changes/).

item: RESOLVED in part 2026-10-18: whose/what income counts toward $580; REMAINING: gross-vs-net for rent & Kalshi gains
value: Individual's total gross income (ACWDL 25-30); gross-vs-net for rental/trading = blank/unverified
detail: Update 2026-10-18 (session af61680c): DHCS ACWDL 25-30 (preliminary county guidance, Dec 30 2025) resolves the earlier gap: the test is the individual's total gross income, assessed individually (one person's compliance cannot satisfy another's), and fluctuating-income averaging expressly includes earned income, unemployment, SDI, retirement income, dividends, etc. What remains unverified: ACWDL does not state whether rental income is counted as gross rents or net Schedule E profit, nor how Kalshi event-contract gains (gross proceeds vs net gain) are counted. Do not assume - confirm the county's verification method before relying on rent/trading to clear $580 in a given month.
notes: Supersedes earlier 'not confirmed from a California official source' note. ACWDL is preliminary and may change with final CMS guidance.

item: DHCS copay income figure does not match current FPL
detail: The DHCS member page says the October 1, 2028 Medi-Cal copays apply to adults making more than $15,560 a year. That figure matches neither the 2025 ($15,650) nor the 2026 ($15,960) 100% FPL guideline for one person. Flagged as a possible typo or reference to a different standard in DHCS member materials.

value: 2027 HHS poverty guidelines not yet published as of the snapshot
detail: HHS publishes new guidelines each January; healthcare.gov notes that 2027 income levels for marketplace savings publish November 1, 2026. 2027 subsidy thresholds in this site therefore use the 2026 guidelines ($15,960 for one person), consistent with Covered California's July 2026 release (e.g., 200% FPL = $31,920). Update when the 2027 guidelines publish.
